messages.content: Return only JSON matching the contract. Review one proposed provider-side tender precondition; do not decide any award, customer usefulness, price, priority, or admission. Existing Node ESM function missingTenderTerms checks content-addressed lot identity, purpose-owning customer, requested changes, productContract shape (type plus unique nonempty required/prohibited/binding/validation arrays), roots, source digests, replay commands, ceilings, authority, effects, and valueAgreement. It currently Offered a historical bad lot: valueAgreement explicitly set staging=false, admission=false, installation=false, but productContract.type was AcceptedSoftwareDeliveryStagingReceipt+SoftwareDeliveryAdmissionReceipt and requiredFields were staging.type, staging.proposedProduct, staging.stagedTreeDigest, admission.type, admission.stagingReceipt, admission.grantDigest, etc. Human review found that contract described future receiver runtime receipts rather than the proposal-only receiver-service artifacts being developed. The corrected good lot retains staging=false/admission=false/installation=false but productContract.type is AcceptedSoftwareDeliveryReceiverServiceProduct; requiredFields are type, serviceIdentity, serviceRoot, operations, artifacts, artifactSetDigest, verificationEntrypoint, selfTestEntrypoint, nonclaims, resourceReceipt; prohibitedFields include stagingCapability, stagingReceipt, admissionGrant, admissionReceipt, installationReceipt; developmentProduct.type exactly matches productContract.type, serviceRoot is the sole ownedTargetRoot, installationState=proposed-only, selfBootstrapInstallationProhibited=true, receiverOwnedAdmissionRequired=true. Candidate gate: return conflicts separately from missing terms; normalize camelCase/dotted field tokens and flag a productContract type or required-field root that positively names staging, admission, or installation when the same valueAgreement boolean is exactly false; additionally, when developmentProduct exists, require its type to equal productContract.type, its serviceRoot to be one ownedTargetRoot, and proposed-only/self-bootstrap fields to agree with false installation terms. Evaluate mechanical fidelity and false-positive risk. Recommend the smallest safer checks that reject the exact bad lot and preserve the exact good lot. Human semantics must remain outside the gate.

structured_output.principalRisk: Check 3's "positively names" is unoperationalized. Substring matching flags incidental occurrences (e.g., PreAdmissionServiceProduct) as false positives. The check is only safe when bound to exact token comparison after splitting productContract.type by camelCase boundaries and required-field paths by dot-path root. Without that bound the gate cannot be adopted.
recommendedChecks: Split productContract.type by camelCase boundaries; raise a CONFLICT if any token is exactly Staging, Admission, or Installation while the corresponding valueAgreement boolean is exactly false.

Split each requiredField by dot-path root (segment before first dot); raise a CONFLICT if that root token is exactly staging, admission, or installation while the corresponding valueAgreement boolean is exactly false.
Treat compound type strings joined by + or / as a set of individual names before token-splitting so a conjunctive type is checked token-by-token, not as an opaque string.
When developmentProduct is present, require developmentProduct.type === productContract.type by exact string equality; raise as a CONFLICT, not a missing term.

When developmentProduct is present and installation is exactly false, raise a CONFLICT if installationState != proposed-only, selfBootstrapInstallationProhibited != true, or receiverOwnedAdmissionRequired != true.
Emit type-vs-valueAgreement conflicts, field-root-vs-valueAgreement conflicts, and missing-term findings as separate named categories so human reviewers can triage without re-parsing output.
unsafeChecks: Do not infer whether staging/admission/installation booleans should be true or false from the type name — that inverts the check direction and encodes customer-usefulness reasoning outside the gate's scope.

Do not apply fuzzy or semantic-similarity matching to type names beyond camelCase token splitting — doing so encodes implicit judgments about which names are semantically adjacent to staging or admission.

Do not validate the contents of effects, ceilings, or authority fields beyond confirming they are non-empty — determining whether those values are correct for the engagement requires human business-rule review.
Do not evaluate whether the prohibitedFields set is correct or complete for a given product type — selecting which fields to exclude is a product-design judgment, not a mechanical coherence check.
